title: Walnut and Parsley Pesto
description: This walnut and parsley pesto tastes a lot like garlic butter, and ideally it should be made in a mortar and pestle. Use on toasted bread, pizza or pasta, or on roasted chicken--it's that versatile!
ingredients: 1 large pinch kosher salt, plus more to taste

steps.text: Place garlic and salt in a mortar; smash and mash with the pestle until it becomes a paste, 5 to 8 minutes. Add walnuts; mash walnuts into a paste until you reach your desired texture (coarse or smoother), another 5 to 8 minutes. Add parsley and mash to break up and blend with the walnut/garlic mixture, about 4 minutes. Add lemon juice and olive oil; stir, mash, and emulsify liquids into the mixture until it becomes very thick and well blended, 8 to 10 minutes. Taste and adjust seasonings. If mixture seems too thick, whisk in a tablespoon of water, or as needed.
Spread on bread, use on pizza or pasta, or on roasted chicken. The taste is just like garlic butter, so use it as such.

video.description: Forget the recipes. Pesto is a simple technique that everyone can do. All you need to add garlicky goodness to all sorts of your favorite dishes is grab your mortar & pestle. Crush garlic and salt into a paste, then add raw walnut and crush those, too. Add cut basil, lemon juice and olive oil and . . . you guessed it, crush some more, which in this case means the mixture will become a semi-smooth paste that’s perfect for spreading on toasted bread, pizza, pasta, roasted chicken, potatoes and more.
